thread_persistence_findings.verdict: ALREADY DURABLE in the canonical repo - not the feared defect.
thread_persistence_findings.where_stored: Memory/oracle_memory.db (SQLite), table 'messages' (session_id, role, content, timestamp). Helpers in core/memory.py.
thread_persistence_findings.saved_immediately: Yes. Main chat path saves the user turn BEFORE the model call (oracle_server.py:2348 save_message user). Assistant turn saved after generation.
thread_persistence_findings.user_turn_survives_timeout: Yes on the main path (user saved before model). Streaming path oracle_server.py:1475-1477 bundles user+assistant after reply - a minor gap if that path times out (see remaining_gaps).
thread_persistence_findings.thread_id_survives_refresh: Yes. GET /api/history (oracle_server.py:3515) returns live _history, else falls back to the most recent durable session.
thread_persistence_findings.refresh_reloads_thread: Yes. ui/index.html init() calls restoreHistory() (line 2467) which fetches /api/history and replays the thread on every page load.
thread_persistence_findings.frontend_only_in_memory: No. There is server-side durable persistence + rehydrate; the in-browser state is just a view.
thread_persistence_findings.localStorage_used: No - and not needed; durability is server-side SQLite, which is stronger.
thread_persistence_findings.root_cause_of_perceived_amnesia: Running the stale :7777 Google Drive copy (predates the durable-history + restoreHistory fixes), not the canonical :7781. Same stale-copy root cause as TP_017.
